T: Christmas in London. Love all around.
D: Interlinked stories of love play out across London in the weeks before Christmas.
P: Serve the mains when everyone arrives for the school Christmas show.
S: the Prime Minister and Natalie at Downing Street
Shortbread fingers baked at 160C for 25 minutes, half-dipped in dark chocolate, served on a plate next to a pot of tea.
the kid who plays a lobster in the school nativity
Lobster meat tossed with mayo, lemon and chives, piled into small toasted brioche rolls with a pinch of paprika.
Wisconsin buffalo wings and blue cheese
Colin's trip to a bar in Wisconsin

Chicken wings baked at 220C for 45 minutes, tossed in hot sauce melted with butter, with blue cheese dip. Pat 1.5kg chicken wings dry and toss with 1 tbsp baking powder and 1 tsp salt. Bake on a rack over a tray at 220C for 45 minutes, turning once, until crisp. Melt 60g butter with 125ml hot sauce. Mix 100g crumbled blue cheese with 120g sour cream, 2 tbsp mayo, a squeeze of lemon and pepper for the dip. Toss the hot wings in the sauce and serve with the dip and celery sticks.
M: Turkey breast rolled with sage and onion stuffing, roasted at 180C for 90 minutes, with roast potatoes, sprouts and cranberry sauce.
Jamie's French cottage coq au vin
Jamie writing in his cottage in France

Coq au vin of chicken, bacon, mushrooms and red wine simmered 90 minutes, with crusty bread. Brown 1.2kg chicken thigh cutlets in a heavy pot and set aside. Fry 150g bacon lardons, 12 peeled pickling onions and 250g button mushrooms until golden. Stir in 1 tbsp plain flour, then 500ml red wine, 250ml chicken stock, 2 garlic cloves and thyme. Return the chicken, cover and simmer 90 minutes until very tender. Season, scatter with parsley and serve with a warm crusty baguette.
W: Sponge soaked in sherry, layered with raspberry jelly, custard and whipped cream, chilled overnight, topped with berries.
K: Red wine warmed with orange, cinnamon, cloves and honey, never boiled, ladled into mugs.

s.note: the Prime Minister and Natalie at Downing Street
s.how: Beat 250g butter with 100g sugar, then mix in 300g flour and 50g rice flour. Press into a tin and bake at 160C for 25 minutes. Cut into fingers and dip half of each in melted dark chocolate. Serve with tea at Number Ten.

s.note: the kid who plays a lobster in the school nativity
s.how: Toss cooked lobster meat from 2 tails with mayonnaise, lemon zest and chives. Split small brioche buns, toast and pile the lobster in. Dust with a pinch of paprika. Every nativity needs a lobster.

m.how: Fry a chopped onion with sage, mix with breadcrumbs for stuffing. Butterfly a 1.5kg turkey breast, spread, roll and tie. Roast at 180C for 90 minutes with 1kg potatoes. Serve with roasted brussels sprouts and cranberry sauce.

w.how: Cut a sponge cake into cubes, press into a glass bowl and splash with sweet sherry. Pour over raspberry jelly and chill until set. Layer with 500ml custard and whipped cream, chill overnight and top with raspberries.

d.how: Pour a bottle of red wine into a pot with a sliced orange, 2 cinnamon sticks, 4 whole cloves and 2 tbsp honey. Warm gently for 20 minutes without boiling. Ladle into mugs on Christmas Eve.
